"Away" means long leave, a trip and so on — not working that half-day (excluded from the specialty-duty candidates; it does not affect the next-day rules for night shifts or on-call, so declare unavailability separately if the night is impossible too). Unavailable / avoid: "day and night" blocks that day's day and night shifts and their on-call (not duty carried from the previous night; if you are unavailable from the small hours, mark the previous day too); "day" blocks only the day shift and its on-call; "night" blocks the night shift and night on-call starting that day (a date-only declaration means this). Wish = a request for that night. Fixed = this person must take that slot (the author's decision; on days off the day and the night can be fixed separately, so combinations such as a day shift plus night on-call are possible; two people cannot hold the same slot). "Avoid …" = a day to avoid if possible (a soft goal: work and on-call in that half-day are avoided with a penalty, but if the declarer's own count would fall below the reference solution — computed ignoring those days — a large penalty applies, so declaring does not reduce their load. For a weekday preference, say "weekday nights on Wednesday", mark the other weekdays' nights as "avoid: night". Weekday patterns of "avoid …" expand on weekdays only; days off are set individually here. On weekdays only the night can be chosen. Being away during a weekday is declared as "Away" in the morning or afternoon field).

about.title: About this app
about.html:
Toban Roster builds a monthly duty roster or shift schedule from your facility's rules — which rules are required, which are soft goals, and how much each goal weighs — and writes it as a Word document (docx) and an explanatory report (HTML). It is a single HTML file, used by departments with on-call duty, two-shift wards with day and night shifts, and other facilities, each choosing its own rules.

The solver (HiGHS, an integer-programming solver compiled to WebAssembly) runs inside the page; nothing is sent over the network, and no AI model is involved. The name comes from the Japanese tōban, "the person on duty".

The rosters this app produces are the result of a computation, not a staffing decision. Have the person in charge review and correct them before use. The software is provided "as is" under the MIT License; the authors accept no liability for damage arising from its use or its results.

Source identifier: /*__SRC_STAMP__*/ (made by build.py from the contents of src, so you can tell whether this file matches a given source tree)

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.html:
• Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome. Opening the file directly (double-click, file://) works.
  • The browser needs WebAssembly, folder access (the File System Access API) and downloads. If an organisation policy blocks folder access, use the JSON download / load on the settings tab instead.
  • Folder permission has to be granted each time the page is opened. The start screen asks for it when you press Start.

folders.title: Folders and saving
folders.html:
Choose a save folder on the start screen. Each month gets its own folder named YYYYMM:

Roster/                          ← the save folder (put toban.html here too)
  toban.html
  plugins/                       ← facility plug-ins, if any (rules/ calendars/ docx/ lang/ profiles/)
  202611/
    202611_data.json             ← input, roster of people, result and version history
    202611_roster_v1_draft.docx  ← the roster (draft or final)
    202611_report_v1_draft.html  ← the report
  • While a folder is connected, the data file is saved automatically a few seconds after each change. When a solve succeeds, the roster docx and the report are written as well.
  • The docx and report are never overwritten: each new assignment or label adds a new version (v1, v2, …). The previous data file is kept as …_data_prev.json.
  • Editing from several PCs: if another PC saved the same month first, the app notices on opening and before saving, and merges both sides' changes item by item, using the last version you saw as the common base. It only asks when the same item was changed on both sides.
  • Avoid editing the same month on two computers at the same time; take turns (the merge is per item, so touching the same item simultaneously means more questions, and overlapping saves can drop one side's change).

facility.title: Setting up your facility
facility.html:
The settings tab has two modes. When a facility starts using the app, decide its shape once under Build the facility profile; day to day, adjust the roster and the strength of the rules under Daily settings. Each change can be undone one step at a time with the "Undo" button.

Build the facility profile (top to bottom)

  1. Starting point. Load the closest bundled facility profile. Bundled: weekday day shifts + night duty (physician sample: duty, on-call, weekend period charge), general duty (minimal), two-shift (one person each on day and night), two-shift nursing ward (4 on nights, 12–13 on days; composition by juniors, leaders and managers, exact days off, post-night days). Give your own shape a name and an identifier and export it to share with other facilities or load it later; unless "include the roster as is" is ticked, the export keeps only roles and targets in the roster, replaces names with role-plus-number placeholders, leaves out years, qualifications and per-person conditions, and warns before writing if a name still remains in a text.
  2. Calendar. The source of public holidays (a bundled calendar or a plug-in one) and facility closure days. Fixed-assignment tags (training, meeting… — the reason an assignment was fixed) and day categories (events etc., shown as columns in the per-day table of the monthly conditions) are set here too.
  3. Parts of the day and the shifts to compute. Name the daytime and the night, and decide which days are computed (never / weekends and holidays only / weekdays only / every day) and how many people fill one slot. The count may be a range (e.g. 12–13).
  4. Roles. Give each role an identifier and a display name, and, if a rule needs to refer to it, choose its function in the rules (can hold period charge / paired role / assists / reserve, normally not assigned). One name in the language your facility uses is enough.
  5. On-call (standby). Whether standby staff are decided in addition to the workers, which shifts get them, and how many per worker role.
  6. Facility plug-ins. Plug-ins loaded from plugins/ in the save folder (or built into the file) are listed per file (kind, where it was loaded from, the rules, day categories, layouts and calendars it registered). Untick a file to treat its rules, day categories, calendar extension, layouts and calendars as absent (for checking; tick again to restore).
  7. Rules in use. Tick the rules your facility uses. Unticked rules are used neither for solving nor for verification. Rules from plug-ins carry a "plug-in" tag and their source, and a warning appears when two rules that cover the same thing are both in use.
  8. Output. The docx layout (the bundled week block on A3 portrait or the month table, plus plug-in layouts), paper size and orientation.

Daily settings

  • Roster. Name, role, years of experience, qualifications, whether the person takes duty, and so on. Columns used by only one rule appear only while that rule is in use. The qualifications column lists, as checkboxes, the qualifications written in the composition rule.
  • Rules. Only the rules in use are listed. Make each one "required" (no solution when it cannot be kept) or "penalised" (avoided by weight), and set the rule's values (run lengths, how days off are counted, composition conditions…). "The rules as they read with the current settings" above is the same text as section 0 of the report and is generated from the settings (rules from plug-ins are marked [plug-in]).

monthly.title: Each month
monthly.html:
1. In the month list in the header, choose + Create next month. The carry-over from the end of last month (the last few days where run-length rules are used), running totals and weekday patterns marked to carry forward are brought across.
  2. 1 Month → Month: holidays (can be filled in from the facility's calendar), this month's target counts, and anything already fixed.
  3. 1 Month → Per-person calendar: for each person, unavailable days, paid leave, days to avoid if possible, wishes, fixed assignments and, where used, daytime duties. Fixed assignments lets you enter everything already decided, slot by slot.
  4. 2 Solve. The input is checked first and any contradiction is reported by name with a suggested fix — including how many days are off when the head count does not match the slots. If there is no solution, the conflicting rules are diagnosed.
  5. 3-1 Result shows the verification and totals; 3-2 shows each person's calendar, with post-night days and days off. The status line at the top of the result gathers the four things you need to decide whether to adopt it: saved or not, solved from the current input or not, verification with the current settings (violations and allowances due to fixed assignments), and whether optimality is proven or the time ran out. Set the label to Final when the roster is agreed.
  6. To adjust after publishing, solve again with Keep the current result and change as little as possible (on by default). Changed slots are shown in red in the docx and the report.

"Days to avoid if possible" are avoided by penalty. A penalty also applies when the person's shift count falls below what it would be without the request, so requests are unlikely to reduce anyone's load (this is a penalty, not a guarantee).

trouble.title: Troubleshooting
trouble.html:
• "Could not save to the folder": reading or writing the folder failed (a disconnected share, another program holding the file). The input is still in the browser; fix the cause and press Save now in the header.
  • No solution: first read the input check at the top of the solve log. Common causes in a new facility: the head count does not match the slots (with days off set to "exactly", even one day off makes it unsolvable — adjust with paid leave or a range of people per slot), too few people meet a composition condition, or two rules contradict each other (for example, forbidding consecutive working days while also requiring runs of at least three). If the input check is silent, the diagnosis lists the conflicting rules and, where it can, the person, date or fixed assignment.
  • Solving takes long: raise the time limit on the solve tab. Rosters with several people per slot have many equally good solutions and benefit from a longer limit.
  • The input looks wrong: an old browser state may remain. Connect the folder and choose to load the folder's data when asked.
  • Too many settings changed: the Undo button on the settings tab reverts them one at a time (while the page is open).

developers.title: For developers
developers.html:
• The source is webapp/src/*.js; build.py assembles toban.html (the "source stamp" above identifies it). build.py --check verifies the cross-references between the UI files and that no names outside the roster remain in the sample data.
  • model.js reads the input and holds the rule states; rules-core.js and rules/*.js hold the rules (one rule per file, with the solver side solve, the verification check and the penalty recount penalty written separately); solver.js builds the integer program; check.js is the verification framework and the input check; report.js the report; docxgen.js the docx; plugins.js the loader for facility plug-ins. To add a rule, add one file under rules/ and write its messages in English first (design: docs/rule-modules.md).
  • Facility plug-ins: files placed under plugins/ in the save folder (rules/ calendars/ docx/ lang/ profiles/) are loaded when the folder is connected. Besides rules they can register day categories (T.dayFlags.register), per-person calendar extensions (T.calendarExt.register: fixed-assignment tags, symbols, legend, day headers), calendars, docx layouts, translations and profiles. build.py --plugins <folder> bakes them into a single file. How to write them, with samples: plugin-example/README.md in the repository.
  • run_tests.sh runs the whole suite: the regression baseline (golden), agreement of the penalties counted by the solver side and by the verification side (the sample facility, settings with changed rule states, corrupted assignments), exhaustive search over a few emptied slots against the optimum, the plug-in loader, and the cross-check against the Python / CP-SAT version in tools/ (default configuration only).
  • Languages: UI strings are looked up by their Japanese text in i18n.js. Violation and input-check messages live in messages.js as a code plus values, English first. Add a language by adding one lang/<code>.json.
  • docx layouts: register with T.docx.register(id, render, {label}) and the layout appears in the settings tab.
  • Design notes are in docs/ of the repository.
